about.title: Carmel Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Carmel's charm comes with narrow, tourist-heavy streets, and recent public records show 7 injury collisions and 7 people hurt in a single year, with no reported traffic deaths. Crashes tend to cluster on Fridays around midday, often along Ocean Avenue, San Carlos Street, Junipero Avenue, and the southbound stretch of SR-1 (Cabrillo Highway), where local traffic mixes with visitors unfamiliar with the roads. If you were injured in one of these collisions, sorting out fault, insurance calls, and medical bills can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover money for you. Reaching out early can help preserve evidence while details are still fresh.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public vehicle — was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your Carmel accident before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you — even if you were mostly not at fault. Insurers often try to shift blame early, so it helps to have someone reviewing the facts on your side before you respond.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Hurt Your Claim
items.desc: The other driver's insurance company may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, but anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. An attorney can advise you on what to say — and what to avoid — while working on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get that guidance.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Carmel?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a city-owned vehicle or a road defect, played a role, that deadline can be much shorter — sometimes just six months. Because these timelines are strict, it's worth having an attorney review your situation as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the crash happened on Ocean Avenue or SR-1 during a busy weekend?
items.answer: Corridors like Ocean Avenue, San Carlos Street, and the southbound stretch of SR-1 see steady public-record collision counts, and weekend or midday traffic can complicate how a crash is documented. Witness statements, traffic camera footage, and business surveillance near these areas can be valuable evidence, so acting quickly to preserve it matters. An attorney connected through LawProactive can help you understand what evidence might still be available.

items.question: Should I speak with the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other side's insurer before speaking with an attorney, since anything you say could be used to reduce your claim under California's comparative fault rules. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney at no cost so you have guidance before any conversation with an adjuster. There's no obligation, and attorneys in the network only get paid if you recover compensation.
